d: Create a character, finish the tutorial on Ancora, build a raft to the Safe House and take your first tasks from K

sec.x: Every new character starts on Ancora — the tutorial island that teaches the first survival steps. Once your Raft is finished you sail to the Safe House, your first base. From there you head out to your Tamed Island and the other islands. Escape raft

Create up to 3 characters per account Watch the prologue or press Skip Pick your character's former job at creation — it gives starting skills and items Learn the basics on Ancora: scanning, gathering, resting, eating Build a raft and depart for the Safe House Take tasks from K and the beginner pioneer tasks that pay T Stone

Launch the game → Select Server (the server list is shown in game) → Create Character Set your appearance, then pick your character's former job in the prologue — it hands out starting skills and items on your first login (see Skills & jobs) You can Skip the opening scene One account holds 3 characters — characters waiting to be deleted still count Deleting a character: it is removed for real after a 24-hour countdown, which you can cancel · a character that is online cannot be deleted For logging in and moving to another PC see Account & login

New characters spawn on Ancora. The guide pops up step by step, and the tasks (the "Ancora" group) run in order: Step   Task   Goal   Reward 1   Try the scan button   Press the magnifier button in the screen corner   30 EXP 2   Logs for the raft   Have 4 Logs   40 EXP 3   Stalks to bind the raft   Have 6 Stalks   40 EXP 4   Leave Ancora   Put the materials into the raft on the beach and depart to the Safe House   120 EXP · 500 T Stone Make a Raft Make a Raft: touch the raft on the beach → put in 4 Logs + 6 Stalks → when complete press Depart Depart → you land at the Safe House The raft is the only way off Ancora — sailing any other way before the raft is done is refused During the tutorial K gives you emergency rations (if you have nothing edible in your bag) The date palms for the food task grow new fruit in 5 seconds, so nobody gets stuck waiting On Ancora, wood/stone/plants come back 4× faster than normal and resting is 3× faster If you log out mid-tutorial you come back to the same spot on Ancora [!tip] No axe yet? Look for fallen logs on the ground, and reeds or tough-stemmed plants near water.

sec.h: 3. The Safe House — your first base
sec.x: The raft lands you at the Safe House (the Company's rest island). It is a safe island: no fatigue from climate or island level, and the weather is mostly sunny (see Weather). What you can do at the Safe House: Talk to K to get the "Tasks from K" chain Take the balloon to pick your own Tamed Island (see Islands) Sail to other islands from the port (see Travel) It is the default return point when the island you were on is not stable (see Death) Tasks from K Task   Goal   Reward Report to K   Talk to K next to her motorbike   50 EXP Firewood for K   Gather 5 items from the trees around the Safe House, then talk to K   120 EXP · 300 T Stone A stone knife for K   Make 1 stone knife and bring it to K   200 EXP · 500 T Stone Stone knife

These can be done anywhere, in any order: Task   Goal   Reward Gatherer   Gather 20 items from nature   60 EXP · 200 T Stone Apprentice   Craft your first item   60 EXP · 200 T Stone Building a home   Build your first structure   80 EXP · 300 T Stone Hunter   Hunt 3 animals   80 EXP · 300 T Stone First friend   Tame 1 animal   100 EXP · 500 T Stone A pioneer's first step   Reach level 5   1,000 T Stone After these, a long story chain runs up to level 60 — see Tasks & story.

d: Life, Health, Energy and Fatigue gauges · resting, drinking and washing · body temperature and getting too cold or too hot

sec.x: Every island in Durango wears you down — fatigue piles up from work and climate, walking burns Energy, and your body temperature follows the weather. This page explains the gauges on screen, how to recover, and the server's real numbers.

d: Weather changes every 20 minutes per island · seasons turn every 7 days · the Unstable Index (1–10) makes islands harsher and needs a Climate Resistance Level before you can sail there

sec.x: Every island has its own weather based on its terrain (tropical forests rain often, deserts bake, snow fields snow), and the weather has real effects: you walk slower, predators see you from closer, rain waters your crops, storms put out fires. Unstable islands also carry an Unstable Index: the higher it is, the more dangerous — and the more rewarding.

Check the current weather on the on-screen clock and plan your trips Let the rain water your fields · sit out storms in a shelter Pick an island by its Index on the sailing screen Build up your Climate Resistance Level by staying on islands of that climate, to unlock high-Index islands

d: Life at zero = death · half the items in your bag drop where you died, recoverable for 5 minutes · revive at a warp hole, your waypoint, the landing point or on the spot (free) · friends can give you CPR

sec.x: When your Life reaches 0 your character dies. Some of the items in your bag drop at the spot where you died, and you choose where to revive. This page covers what you lose, how to get it back, and this server's spawn rules.

Revive at a Warp Hole you have discovered · your Waypoint on this island · or the island's landing point Instant Revival on the spot where you died (currently free) Let another player give you CPR, and set a thank-you gift for them Walk back and pick up your dropped items within 5 minutes Lock important items in your bag so they never drop

Most statuses are removed on death (Wet, Washed, food buffs, poison…) Fatigue drops depending on how many times you died in a row (the count resets if more than 1 hour passed since your last death) Death number (within 1 hour)   Fatigue removed 1   30% 2   20% 3   10% 4 or more   None

sec.h: Logging out on a temporary island
sec.x: In the original game unstable islands could disappear, so this server decides at login: if you log out or disconnect on a temporary island, your next login puts you at the landing point of your home island (where your waypoint is) if that island is still stable, otherwise at the Safe House, with a message that your previous island is gone. Island you logged out on   Next login Safe House · Ancora · Tamed Island · villages/cities · Index 1 islands   Same place Index 2 and up islands · event islands · training island · islands that were closed   Home island → otherwise Safe House Your items and pets all come with you Just arriving on a temporary island does not move you — only logging back in after really leaving the game does Leaving an island by any means clears your checkpoint on that island [!tip] Logging off for a long time? Do it on your home island, your Tamed Island or the Safe House — you will come back to the same spot.
Within 12 tiles of an island's port/spawn point no animals spawn and predators do not follow you in — revive at the landing point and you will not be mobbed again.

The original game had after-effects of reviving (dizziness lowering accuracy · reviving with less than full gauges if you die often) — this server does not apply them yet, and is set to always revive with full gauges.

d: Gather plants, wood, stone and ore, and butcher carcasses — item level, success chance, required tools and regrow times

sec.x: Everything on the islands starts with gathering — branches, leaves, stones and ore, all the way to leather and meat from animal carcasses. Every gathered item has a level; the higher the level, the better the things you craft from it. Some pieces also come with latent attributes. Players gathering plants and ore

Plants — leaves, fruit, flowers, reeds, mushrooms and more; most can be picked bare-handed Wood — branches and bark by hand · logs from big trees need an axe or a saw Stone and ore — big stones, ore and gems need a pickaxe or a hammer Dirt — bare hands or a shovel Carcasses — hunt an animal, then butcher it for leather, meat and bone (Butchering skill category) — see Animals Structures that produce items — such as wells or traps, harvested in rounds — see Building

Walk up to the resource (within 3 tiles) and tap it The menu lists what you can gather there, with the level you will actually get Pick an entry — the game picks a suitable tool for you; entries you have no usable tool for are grayed out Wait for the progress bar to fill, then see the result: Success · Flawless Success · or Failed to Gather If your Energy is low, the game asks whether you want to continue Some categories need a skill first — tapping them opens the skill page for the skill you need

sec.h: Stone and ore come back on time
sec.x: Every entry on the same resource has its own timer — someone else taking a different entry from the same rock does not restart the timer you are waiting on Stone and ore always come back on time; plants may take longer if the area already has as many plants as its ecosystem allows
New characters' first island is tuned for practising gathering and crafting: natural resources are ×4 denser · grow back 4× faster (season table above) · resting recovers ×3 faster

Each successful gather gives skill-category experience (Gathering / Butchering) based on the level of the item you got compared with your category level: Item level vs category level   Category experience Equal or higher   3 1–5 lower   2 6–15 lower   1 More than 15 lower   0 Flawless Success ×1.5 (rounded up, max 3) · failed gathers give no experience · see Skills

[!tip] Always carry tools at least as high-level as the island you visit — tools above the requirement also add a little success chance. [!tip] High-level items need a high-level character too — gathering on a level 45 island with a Lv20 character only gives Lv20 items. [!tip] A tool with the «Extra Extra» attribute has a 10% chance to give one more item. See Item attributes.

sec.h: Coming soon: one timed action at a time
sec.x: Actions with a progress bar (gathering, butchering, washing, drinking, drawing water, dyeing, taming, crafting and so on) run one at a time Starting a new one before the current bar is full = the new one replaces it, and the old one gives nothing Results arrive only when the bar completes · for gathering, the resource is taken when the bar completes — if someone else takes it first or you walk out of range, you get nothing

d: Craft tools, weapons and clothes and process materials — recipes, workbenches, product level, Processing Chances and desulfurizing metal with seashells

sec.x: What you gather becomes tools, weapons, clothes, food and building parts. Many materials must be processed first (trimmed, smelted, tanned, dried …) before the next recipe accepts them. The level and attributes of your materials carry over into what you make. A recipe's material slots

Craft tools, weapons, clothes, bags, medicine and more from the Craft menu Process materials — the same item is upgraded (it gets a mark showing it was processed) so it fits the next recipe Leave work on a workbench — put a job on the table and go do something else (unattended crafting) Cook — see Cooking and Preserving food Structures use Plans — see Building

Open the Craft menu and pick a Recipe Put Materials into each slot — each slot shows which tags/attributes and levels it needs; items that don't qualify can't be selected Some recipes need you to stand next to the right kind of Workbench, or to hold a specific tool Wait for the progress bar to fill, then collect your item Recipes unlock by learning Skills, and some recipes/Plans unlock by themselves once your Crafting Ability in that category is high enough The recipe page shows the required ability as its difficulty — it does not block crafting right now

Topic   Value Normal crafting time   2 s (skills can shorten it · minimum 0.5 s) Processing time   per recipe, at most 20 s Stamina used   5 per craft Crafting failure   none — you always get the item Flawless Success   10% Product level   average level of all materials, rounded down (capped at the recipe's max level) Level of a processed item   same as the original item Flawless Success puts a «Flawless Success» mark on the item · +10% max durability · processing recipes give +1 level to the attributes they add · ×1.5 experience

Each craft gives experience in the recipe's skill category (Weapon/Tool Crafting · Tailoring · Cooking · Build · Processing) based on the product level compared with your category level — the same table as Gathering.

Supported recipes (such as smelting ore and desulfurizing metal at a kiln) can be left on a Workbench — materials are taken right away and the item waits on the table until the time is up Each recipe has its own wait time (at least 5 s) · you can't use someone else's workbench without permission · a full workbench takes no more jobs A workbench built from a material with «Splits Easily» may get «More Space» (+1 slot) or «Shorter Duration» (−5% unattended time) — see Item attributes

A weapon assembled from parts Processing doesn't turn the item into a new one — it adds tags/attributes to the same piece, and the next recipe checks those tags. Examples: Recipe   Takes   Result Trimmed Material   bone, stone, wood   trimmed tag → usable for blades/handles Compressed Material   a trimmed item + water   processed tag + extra attributes Refined Ore   ore + charcoal   becomes a metal chunk Desulfurized Metal   metal chunk + 2 charcoal + 2 seashells   gains «High Purity» Dry Leather   leather / fur   gains «Dried» Fiber-Tanned Material   dried leather + bark + leaves   tans the leather · removes bad smell Waterproofed Material   leather / fabric + fat   gains «Waterproof» Long Strap   2 strings (vines, thread or sinew also work)   long-string tag → can make bowstrings Plank   a pillar/log   becomes a plank

Every item has 3 Processing Chances Recipes that show the line «Processing Chance Consumed» use 1 chance from the item in the main slot — 77 recipes: almost all processing recipes + 8 regular recipes (their product inherits the main item's remaining chances −1) Dyeing does not use a chance · bleaching uses 1 At 0 the item can't be processed any more — the game says so (server message in Thai) Modifying gear costs Modification Slots instead of Processing Chances

Metal with powder and metal with a seashell The pure-metal chain: ore → Refined Ore (ore + charcoal) → Desulfurized Metal (metal chunk + 2 charcoal + 2 Seashell seashells) → the metal chunk gains «High Purity» The level of «High Purity» equals the item's level — 17 recipes for advanced metal blades and metal bow/crossbow stocks ask for level 35 or 55 «Waterproof» (Waterproofed Material) and «Dried» (drying recipes) follow the same rule Metal you desulfurized before this fix works right away — no need to redo it
The material in the main slot passes its attributes on to what you craft (each one can be lost at every step) — details in Item attributes.
Tools and weapons wear out with use; repair them with a Repair Kit or T Stone — see Decay and repair.

[!tip] Product level is the average of every material — one low-level secondary material can drag the result down. [!tip] Plan your processing chain before you start — each item can only be processed 3 times. [!tip] Long jobs like smelting and desulfurizing can be left at a kiln while you go gathering.

d: Latent and rare (green) attributes — how you get them while gathering, how they carry over when crafting, and what each one does

sec.x: Each material may come with attributes such as «Firm», «High Density», or green ones like «Black Sheen». When you craft, the attributes of the material in the main slot become attributes of the product — more attack, more durability, or special effects like bleeding. A sword with special attributes

Open Item Info for the item Attributes show as chips  with their level — the color tells how rare they are: Color   Meaning Green   Rare Attribute — a special effect Yellow   a good attribute Normal   a basic attribute Gray   a negative attribute Tap a chip to read its description · combat/gathering rare attributes have no number on the stats page — read the chip's description instead

d: Build a field or flower bed, plant seeds, water and fertilize them, then harvest the crop plus one seed back

sec.x: Grow your own plants on fields you build. Crops grow in real time, even while you are offline. Once a crop is ripe you pull it up to get the produce (food, flowers, fiber and more) plus one seed back. Planting a seed

Build a Small Field / Large Field or a Flower Bed and plant one seed per plot Give Water and Give Fertilizer to shorten the growing time (optional — an unwatered crop still grows, just slower) Place a Sprinkler to water many plots at once without using water from your bag Harvesting gives Farming skill exp and levels up that seed's Farming Encyclopedia entry, which unlocks specializations

Build a plot (see Building). sec.h: Some produce is still a generic item
sec.x: For 21 crops the original game's specific produce is unknown, so they currently give a generic item instead, e.g. ornamental flowers → Flower · Maple Tree/Ginkgo Tree → Leaf · Banana Tree, Mango, Orange → Tropical Fruit · Fig Tree → Normal Fruit. This may change once more data is found.

d: Eat to refill energy and get buffs and taste bonuses — a hidden satiety meter stops you from binge-eating

sec.x: Food is your character's main source of Energy. Besides energy, some foods restore health, give stat buffs, help against heat or cold, or boost the exp you earn when they taste good — but you can't binge-eat, because a hidden "satiety" meter holds you back. Eating

Eat food from your bag → get its full energy right away, plus the food's other effects Drink Water at a river, lake or sea shore without needing a bottle or item Eat tasty food to get the Delicious status (more exp) and foods that give the Enhanced Ability buff Cook before eating to avoid Stomach Pain from raw food (see Cooking)

Open your bag, pick a food and choose Eat (drinks: Drink) — your character plays an eating animation, then the effect applies Stand next to water and choose Drink Water — takes 5 seconds and gives +5 energy and the Water status, same as drinking a bottle of water, without using an item If you eat a different buff food while a food buff is still active, the game asks "Previous food's effect will disappear. Continue?" — confirm and the new buff replaces the old one

There is no satiety bar on screen, but the server tracks it in the background: Every food has its own satiety value, added when you eat it Satiety caps at 100 and digests steadily, from 100 down to empty in 30 minutes While you are below 100 you can always eat, even if that bite takes you over 100 Once you reach 100 you get the Full status and can't eat; the game tells you roughly how many seconds/minutes to wait Dying or levelling up removes Full immediately Drink Water from a water source does not count toward satiety Food   Satiety per piece   Pieces until Full (from empty)   Steady rate (pieces/hour) Water   5   20   40 Apple · Minnow · Egg · Raspberry   10   10   20 Meat Kebab   12   9   16.7 Bread · Meat-Stuffed Bread · Sashimi · Root   15   7   13.3 Meat   20   5   10 Tenderloin Steak   50   2   4 Fat   120   1   1.7

Eating raw food also cancels Delicious.

Gathering, crafting and other work cost energy. If you have less energy than an action needs, the game warns you first and lets you choose to eat first or carry on — for the energy and fatigue gauges see Survival.

[!tip] Grill meat with the Skewer recipe before eating — same energy, but no Stomach Pain and you get Delicious (exp ×1.03). [!tip] High-satiety foods (Fat, steak) fill you up fast. If you need lots of energy, pick foods with high energy but low satiety, such as Apple. [!tip] You can only have one Enhanced Ability buff at a time — don't accidentally eat a different buff food over the one you want.

d: Cook ingredients at a bonfire or kitchen — removes rawness and adds heat/cold, flavor and special properties per recipe

d: Fight animals bare handed, with melee weapons, bows or crossbows — damage depends on weapon attack, the move you use, and armor penetration against the animal's defense

sec.x: Dinosaurs and wild animals are your food, your materials and your biggest danger. Combat on this server follows the original game's rules: every hit starts from weapon attack × the move's multiplier, then compares your armor penetration with the animal's defense. The colored area an animal draws on the ground while winding up is exactly where it will hit — step out in time and it misses. A hunter slashing a raptor

Fight bare handed, with one-handed weapons (axe · knife/sword · blunt weapon), two-handed weapons, spears, bows and crossbows Use heavy hits, flurries and sweeping moves that hit several animals at once (these must be learned from the combat skill tree — see Skills) Stagger an animal so the attack it is winding up is cancelled; make it stunned / collapse to capture it (see Taming) Break body parts (head · body · legs · tail) to slow an animal down or weaken its attacks Use green weapon tags to make animals bleed (see Tags)

Tap an animal to target it, then press Attack  — your character walks into range and swings A weapon's basic attack is always available · special moves (heavy hit, flurry, stab, sweep, strike, aimed shot, quick shot) must be learned first Watch the colored area under the animal while it winds up — run out of it before the attack lands to dodge Animals you hit will turn and fight; some herbivores run away instead (see Wild animals)

Numbers are the move's damage multiplier (1.0 = normal hit) · several numbers = several strikes Weapon   Normal hit   Special moves (multiplier) Bare Handed (attack 40)   1.0   Kick 0.8 · heavy hit 1.3 · punch combo 0.6 ×3 One-Handed (axe · knife/sword · hammer)   1.0   Heavy hit 2.2 · flurry 0.9 / 1.1 / 1.33 · stab 2.8 Two-Handed   1.0   Heavy hit 2.2 · sweep 1.1 / 1.6 · strike 2.5 Spear   1.0   Heavy thrust 2.2 · dash thrust 1.1 ×3 Bow / Crossbow   1.0   Quick shot 1.0 / 1.0 / 1.22 · aimed shot 2.1 [!note] Holding a weapon uses the weapon's attack only (the bare-hand 40 is not added) · axes, swords and hammers share the same move multipliers; they differ in their mastery skills

Damage = weapon attack × move multiplier × penetration multiplier × direction multiplier × critical Penetration multiplier = 2.2 to the power of ((weapon armor penetration − animal defense) ÷ 100) Difference 0 = ×1 · penetration ahead by 100 or more = ×2.2 (cap) · defense ahead by 100 or more = ×0.45 (floor) Animal defense grows with level (usually level × 5, e.g. Raptor Lv10 = 50) and is multiplied by the island's Unstable Index Hit chance = 50% + move accuracy × 45% (normal moves = 95%) · heavy moves −4% · always between 35% and 99% Critical hit chance 10% (heavy moves 18%) · damage ×1.9 Examples (hit from the front, no critical) Weapon   Move   Target   Damage per hit Bare Handed   Normal   Compsognathus Lv1   42 Bare Handed   Normal   Raptor Lv10   30 Stone Axe Lv15   Normal   Raptor Lv10   95 Stone Axe Lv15   Heavy hit   Raptor Lv10   209 Bone Knife Lv15   Stab   Sabertooth Lv40   94 Bone Bow Lv30   Normal shot   Raptor Lv10   163 [!tip] Animals far above your weapon's level hit the ×0.45 floor and barely take damage — upgrade your weapon so its penetration keeps up before visiting high-level islands

Every hit adds "blow power" to the animal's gauge. When the gauge reaches the species' stagger resistance, the animal staggers and the attack it is winding up is cancelled, then the gauge starts over · if it isn't hit for 4 seconds, the gauge resets Blow power per hit   Value Bow · bare hand · one-handed · crossbow (normal hit)   60 · 80 · 90 · 100 Two-handed (normal hit) · heavy hit · stab   120 · 150 · 180 Two-handed strike / second sweep swing   240 Animal   Resistance   One-handed normal hits needed Compsognathus · Phenacodus   140   2 Raptor   420   5 Sabertooth · Direwolf   560   7 Mammoth   1,120   13 Tyrannosaurus   1,575   18

Every move has its own hit area (circle · cone · rectangle) and the server checks each hit against it Area moves (flurry · sweep · stab · strike · punch combo) can hit several animals at once, up to 6 per swing Animal attacks are cones/rectangles taken from their real moves (e.g. a raptor's tail swipe hits behind it) · the yellow/red area on screen = where the hit really lands

Direction: most animals take ×0.8 from the front · ×1.0 from the sides · ×1.2 from behind (Tyrannosaurus is reversed: front ×1.2 · back ×0.8) · you also take ×1.2 when an animal hits you from behind Body parts: each hit lands on the head/body/legs/tail at random depending on the direction. Each part has its own health; when it breaks: Broken legs → the animal walks/runs at 60% speed and is easier to hit Broken head or tail → the animal hits weaker or misses more often Broken parts heal by themselves after 10 minutes · when butchering, items from broken parts come out halved (except meat) Axe mastery skills add +6% body-part damage per level

Some green tags on weapons/gear make animals bleed (health drains over time — if it dies you get a normal carcass) or make animals that hit you miss more often · bleeding does not stagger or stun · see Tags for the tag list

Animals use the same formula: animal attack × 2.2 to the power of ((animal penetration − your total armor defense) ÷ 100) · armor reduces damage but never blocks it completely; high-level animals hit very hard Animal   Your total defense   Damage taken Raptor Lv10   0   35 Raptor Lv10   50   24 Sabertooth Lv40   100   176 Mammoth Lv50   150   466 Tyrannosaurus Lv60   300   952 [!warn] Animals Lv40 and above can kill a lightly armored player in 1–3 hits — go as a team, use heavy moves to stagger, and dodge the colored areas in time
Hitting an animal repeatedly drains its stun gauge until it freezes (stunned) or collapses with stars over its head. It can't attack during that time and can be captured — see Taming
Players cannot fight each other · your only enemies are animals
The accuracy stat on weapons and the animals' evasion are not used for hit chance yet (hit chance comes from the move only) · knockback moves have no push effect

d: Animal temperaments, island-based levels, herds and alphas, predators hunting prey, movement/sleep, and what you get from butchering

sec.x: Every island is home to herds of dinosaurs and prehistoric animals. Some attack the moment they see you, some run, some ignore you until they are hit. Animals have levels based on their island, sleep at night, hunt each other in front of you, and leave a carcass you can butcher for meat, leather and bones. Raptor Tyrannosaurus Sabertooth Mammoth

Hunt animals and butcher their carcasses into materials (see Combat) Capture animals to raise as pets (see Taming) Challenge the alpha of each island Watch predators hunt prey · sneak past animals sleeping at night

Temperament   Behavior Aggressive   Sees you within 8 tiles → notices you in 2.5 seconds (alphas 1.5) → roars and chases · gives up once more than 32 tiles from home Neutral   Ignores you until hit, then fights back Skittish   Runs away when hit or when a predator comes After 20 seconds out of combat, animals regenerate 0.3% health per second · Tyrannosaurus and Apatosaurus regenerate 1% per second · Allosaurus does not regenerate [!tip] If you hit an animal and then leave it alone for a long time, it heals back — keep the pressure on when hunting big animals

Regular animals spawn at island level ±5 (minimum 1 · maximum 70) · alphas and elite leaders keep the fixed level from the spawn table Health, attack and defense grow with level using the original game's formula (health ≈ species constant × (level + 24)²) The same species at different levels can differ a lot in toughness — that is real game data, not a bug Animal   Lv10   Lv20   Lv30   Lv60 Raptor (health)   488   817   —   — Sabertooth (health)   1,053   1,764   2,656   6,428

On an Unstable Island the health and attack of every animal (alphas included) are multiplied by 1 + (Unstable Index − 1) × 0.25 · the level shown over its head does not change Unstable Index   1   3   4   7   10 Multiplier   ×1   ×1.5   ×1.75   ×2.5   ×3.25

Public islands hold about 9 animals per 64×64-tile area (3 herds × 3 animals), using the species from that island's table Every island keeps at least 3 herds with ≥ 3 animals each — if hunting drops it below that, the missing herd returns to its spot after 3 minutes (aggressive) · 2 minutes (skittish) · 4 minutes (neutral) Safehouses, tutorial islands and peaceful islands are not topped up Areas with nobody around for 30 minutes put their herds to rest; when someone returns, the remaining animals come back

Most islands have one alpha per alpha species (e.g. the Alpha Tyrannosaurus). Alphas are always aggressive and never sleep Topic   Value Health   ×2.5 of the same species (at least 2,000 + 50 × level) Elite leaders   ×1.5 (at least 250 + 12 × level) Respawn at the same spot   30 minutes (elite leaders 10 minutes) Examples   Alpha Tyrannosaurus Lv60 ≈ 389,191 · Allosaurus Lv60 ≈ 96,914 · Elephantulus Lv60 = 5,000 No alphas on Tamed Islands or safehouses · on Unstable Islands their health is multiplied by the Index as well

In areas where players are present, hungry aggressive carnivores actually chase down other animals in front of you They only hunt neutral/skittish animals of a different species and no higher level · alphas neither hunt nor get hunted · players' pets are never hunted Skittish prey runs once the predator is within 8 tiles · neutral prey fights back After a kill the predator eats for 20 seconds, then rests from hunting for 10 minutes · it gives up a chase after 60 seconds The kill leaves a carcass you can butcher, but with half the meat (leather/bones are complete) · no EXP/quest credit since you didn't kill it Hit a predator mid-hunt and it turns on you · a predator already chasing you won't switch to hunting animals At most 2 hunts at a time per area · how often depends on ecosystem hunger (0.08 prey per predator per hour), so it's not common · no hunting on peaceful islands

Running: animals use their real run animation when chasing or fleeing (same speed as before, 0.925 tiles/second · walking 0.575) Sleeping: a game day lasts 48 minutes: dawn (4:30–8) · day (8–17) · dusk (17–21) · night (21–4:30) Night animals (wolves, sabertooths, etc.) are awake at dusk and night · everything else is awake except at night Outside its waking hours each animal has a 45% chance to be asleep (re-rolled daily) · sleeping animals don't wander, chase or hunt They wake if you come within 4 tiles or hit them, then stay awake for 2 minutes · alphas and water animals never sleep Flinching: every hit plays a short flinch (visual only) · only a critical hit or a full stagger gauge interrupts the attack an animal is winding up Roaring: aggressive animals roar the first time they spot you (standing still ≤ 2 seconds) before chasing · alphas roar when a fight starts · once per 60 seconds per animal · no damage · some species have no roar (Sabertooth, Mammoth, Allosaurus, etc.) Stunned/collapsed: see Taming [!tip] Gathering at night on islands with aggressive (non-nocturnal) animals is safer — just don't walk right next to a sleeping one

A dead animal leaves a carcass for 15 minutes (each butchering resets the timer) Tap the carcass → choose a part to butcher, one piece at a time until it's empty · parts you haven't unlocked with butchering skills are greyed out Item level = animal level + your Butchering skill bonus, but never above your character level Animal   Carcass drops (amount per carcass) Compsognathus   Meat 1–2 · Carnivore Leg Bone 1–2 Raptor   Meat 2–3 · Carnivore Leg Bone 1–2 · Leather 1–2 · Teeth 1 Triceratops   Meat 5–8 · Herbivore Leg Bone/Rib 2–3 · Skull 1 · Horn 1–2 · Leather 2–3 Mammoth   Meat 7–10 · Herbivore Leg Bone/Rib 2–3 · Skull 1 · Ivory 1–2 · Pelt 2–3 · Fat 1–2 Tyrannosaurus   Meat 8–12 · Carnivore Leg Bone/Rib 3–4 · Large Skull 1 · Leather 3–4 · Teeth 1 Parts that were broken when the animal died give half (meat excluded) · carcasses left by predators give half the meat

Animals you kill or capture don't pop back at the same spot right away; each area's population regrows over time (only while someone is nearby) · if a species is hunted out of an area, new ones return after the area has been quiet for 12 hours · the 3-herds-per-island minimum always applies
Killing an alpha currently gives the same EXP as a normal animal of the same level (the alpha bonus isn't implemented yet)

d: Beat an animal below 30% health or stun it, then capture it with a Taming Herb — tame it in a pen before forming a bond

sec.x: Almost every wild animal can become your companion. The steps are weaken it → capture it with a Taming Herb → get its Rein → tame it in a pen → form a bond, and you get a pet that travels with you, can be ridden, helps in fights and produces goods. Capturing an animal and putting it in a pen

Capture a wild animal at ≤ 30% health or while it is stunned/collapsed (any health) Use blunt weapons or heavy moves to stun animals faster Tame captured animals in a taming pen, then bond with them as pets

Item   Level   Used for Novice Taming Herb   1–19   Capture tool — must be in your bag Standard Taming Herb   20–39   〃 Advanced Taming Herb   40–60   〃 Makeshift Taming Pen / Small Taming Pen   —   Taming the animals you capture The capture tool loses 3 durability per capture attempt (success or not) · pressing capture before the animal qualifies does not wear the tool

Hit the animal until it has ≤ 30% health or until it is stunned/collapsed (see the stun gauge below) Target it and press Capture  — the button is always pressable when you have a tool; the server checks the conditions Stand still for the 3-second bar (moving cancels) Success → the animal leaves the world and its Rein goes into your bag · failure → a message shows the chance that was rolled; try again after the 5-second cooldown If it doesn't qualify yet, a server message (in Thai) tells you to get its health below 30% or stun it first Carcasses and rift guardians can't be captured · you must stand close · some species can't be captured at all (button locked) [!tip] If you walk away from a low-health animal it can heal back above 30% (it regenerates 20 seconds after combat) — capture quickly

Chance = level factor × (1 − 0.8 × (remaining health ÷ max health)²) · always between 2% and 98% The level factor comes from your character level − the animal's level; the higher you are, the easier · 6 or more levels below the animal = 2% Being stunned/collapsed only allows capture at high health — the chance still uses the real health, with no extra bonus Your level − animal   Health 0%   10%   30%   Stunned, 50% health   Stunned, 80% health   Stunned, full health −6   2%   2%   2%   2%   2%   2% −3   50%   50%   46%   40%   24%   10% 0   80%   79%   74%   64%   39%   16% +3   93%   92%   86%   74%   45%   19% +5   97%   96%   90%   77%   47%   19% +10   98%   98%   92%   80%   49%   20% [!note] The in-game hint says the capture tool's level matters, but on this server the chance uses your character level against the animal's level

Every animal has a stun gauge (for small animals it is roughly 2× their health · multiplied by the island's Unstable Index). Each hit drains it, and the animal moves through these stages Stage   Gauge left   Effect   In-game message Weakened   ≤ ⅓   Warning message only   "… is losing strength." Stunned   ≤ ⅑   Frozen: no attacks, no walking, no fleeing · the attack it was winding up is cancelled   "… is stunned." Collapsed   0   Falls down with stars over its head   "… collapsed!" Recovered   time runs out   Gauge full again   "… steadied itself." A heavy hit can skip from weakened straight to collapsed · you can capture at any moment while it's stunned/collapsed When the fight ends (the animal gives up or returns home) the gauge silently refills · the gauge does not recover by itself mid-fight Animal   Stunned for (seconds)   Collapsed for (seconds) Compsognathus · Phenacodus   6   6 Raptor · Direwolf   8   8 Sabertooth   10   10 Iguanodon   12   12 Triceratops · Mammoth   4   6 Tyrannosaurus   5   3

sec.h: After the capture: taming in a pen
sec.x: Taming pen Build/place a taming pen and put the Rein into it Start taming — it takes 60 seconds · base success chance 60% (maximum 100%) Feed it during taming to help: Food   Effect All-Purpose Taming Feed   Chance +10% · time −30% Fast Taming Feed   Time −50% Meat / Minnow   Time −10 seconds per piece When time is up, collect the result: success → the animal is tamed and gets a random rank (S · A · B · C · D, whichever that species can have) · failure → the animal escapes to the wild and the Rein is lost Use the tamed animal's Rein to form a bond → it becomes your pet (the animal's level must not exceed your Survival category level) — continue at Pets Taming time can't be cut below half [!note] Animal traps give carcass items (meat, leather, bones), not live animals to raise

d: Summon pets to fight, ride and carry items, feed them, use their active skills, produce milk in pens, revive them and keep them from aging

sec.x: Animals you capture and tame become your pets once you form a bond. Summon them to follow you, ride them, carry items in their bag, let them help in fights with their active skill, or put them in a pen to produce milk or train for levels. A bonded pet

Summon / return — one at a time · animals in a pen, roaming, or knocked out can't be summoned Ride — rideable species only (speed depends on species, e.g. Raptor 700 · Mammoth 160) Animal bag — slots depend on species, e.g. Raptor 10 · Sabertooth 30 · Ankylosaurus 150 · Triceratops 240 · Mammoth 300 · Brachiosaurus 500 Feed to restore vigor · rename (1–16 characters) · set free (the animal is gone forever · items in its bag go back to your bag) Roaming — let up to 5 animals roam your Tamed Island (they don't age, can't produce or train · items in their bag disappear) Redraw rank (species with several ranks) — you see the rolled rank first, then accept it or keep the old one

A pet's vigor (300 max for every species) drops only while it is summoned, and is used for fighting, skills and production Species   Vigor lost per second   Full to empty Raptor · Direwolf · Oviraptor · Ornithomimus, etc. (18 species)   0.05   ~100 minutes All other species (83)   0.09   ~55 minutes Food   Vigor restored Leaf · Minnow   40 Meat   50 Nutritious Animal Feed   500 Highly Nutritious Animal Feed   700 Infinite Vigor Feed   Vigor stops dropping for a while Only animal food can be fed (the feeding menu lists it) · a full pet can't eat normal food Attack and Provoke skills need at least half of max vigor (150)

Pet health depends on species and level · pets regenerate 0.3% health per second If wild animals bring it to 0 health the pet is knocked out, returns to your list automatically, and can't be summoned until revived Revive  from the pet screen → full health, vigor at least half

A pet lives for 30 days from bonding, then shows as "Old" — its stats are halved (health, health regen, attack, defense, speed, bag, max vigor, accuracy, etc.) Roaming on your Tamed Island stops the aging clock Animal Anti-Aging Remedy (15/30/45/60 days) gives life time back, but never beyond the full lifespan

Each pet has 1 active skill (37 skills in total) · the first draw is free · redrawing needs a ticket · strength follows the skill's rank (D–S) Type   Examples   Effect Attack   Bite · Rush · Back Kick · Chemical Warfare   The pet hits the target you're fighting (within 6 tiles) for ×2 the pet's attack Provoke   Provoke   Wild animals within 8 tiles go after the pet instead of you Buff   Bared Fangs · Run Free · Strong Back · Healing Helper · Pack Mule   Temporarily raises your pet's or your own stats Skills work while the pet is summoned · each use costs 20 vigor · cooldown depends on the skill (e.g. Bite 15 s · Provoke 33 s · Strong Back 300 s)

A pet and a pen Put a pet in an animal pen (Makeshift Pen · Small Pen · Medium Pen) → choose the pet → Production or Training → wait for the timer, then collect items and pet EXP Production   Time   Vigor used   Pet EXP   Unlocks at pet level Production Lv.1   1 h   150   40   1 Production Lv.2   2 h   170   110   10 Production Lv.3   4 h   190   290   20 Production Lv.4   8 h   270   1,100   30 Production Lv.5   10 h   460   3,900   40 Production Lv.6   12 h   590   15,000   50 Milk comes from production by mammal pets such as Phenacodus, Macrauchenia, Female Megaloceros, Direwolf, Skunkodus: each round gives Milk or Animal Droppings, 50% each Male Megaloceros only gives Animal Droppings · Bumblebee Phenacodus gives Honey 50% / Milk 30% / Animal Droppings 20% Amount per round = (2 + pet level ÷ 10) × the production level's multiplier (1 · 5/3 · 7/3 · 10/3 · 14/3 · 6), rounded down — a Lv1 pet on Production Lv.1 gives 2 9–17% chance of a bonus item (coin · worm · corn seed) · item level = pet level Training Lv.1 takes 1 h and 150 vigor for 100 pet EXP (no items) Production Lv.5–6 needs more than 300 vigor, so raise your pet's max vigor first [!tip] You can feed pets inside the pen (feed button on the pen screen) — top up vigor before starting a new production round

d: Character level, skill categories, skill points, Skill Rewind, the career you pick at character creation, and the Career Guide

sec.x: Your character grows in two ways. Character level goes up from everything you do. Skill categories are separate tracks, and each one only grows from its own kind of work. Character levels give you Skill Points to learn skills. A skill category's level decides which skill ranks you are allowed to learn. Career Guide card for the melee line

Gather, craft, build, hunt and tame to earn character EXP and skill category EXP Spend Skill Points on new skills. Skills give crafting recipes, combat actions and stat bonuses Use Skill Rewind to get points back and learn a different line Pick a career when you create your character. It starts one category at Lv.20 and gives starting items Finish courses in the Career Guide for item rewards and a title

The maximum character level is 60 Doing things at your own level takes about 40 actions (weight 1) per level, at any level EXP also depends on the level of what you do. Lower-level work gives less; higher-level work gives a little more A great success gives ×1.5 Eating, drinking, washing and resting give no EXP Action   Weight (higher = more EXP) Gathering · planting and harvesting   1 Crafting · butchering · dodging an attack · discovering a new spot   2 Building · hunting · capturing/taming   3 The level multiplier is (10 + 2 × level of the thing) ÷ (10 + 2 × your level), at least ×0.1 and at most ×1.5. Example: a Lv.30 character gathering a Lv.10 resource gets about ×0.43. Every character level-up gives +5 Skill Points, +4 max health and +1.5 max energy. Levels 2, 5 and 10 also give a level title.

There are 12 categories you can train. Each goes from Lv.1 to 60 and cannot go above your character level. Once a category catches up with your character level, its EXP bar stays full until your character levels up. Category   Earns EXP from Survival   Capturing/taming animals · discovering new spots or new animal species Melee   Hunting with melee weapons Ranged   Hunting with ranged weapons Defense   Dodging attacks · taking hits Butchering   Butchering carcasses Gathering   Gathering plants, wood, stone and ore (Gathering) Cooking · Weapon/Tool · Tailoring · Processing   Crafting recipes of that category (Crafting) Construction   Building structures (Building) Farming   Planting seeds · harvesting (Farming)

Category EXP per action depends on the level of what you do compared with the category level: Level of the thing vs. category level   Category EXP per action Same or higher   3 1–5 levels lower   2 6–15 levels lower   1 More than 15 levels lower   0 A great success gives ×1.5, but never more than 3 per action Hitting an animal gives EXP in proportion to damage dealt compared with the animal's health Spamming one category far more than normal within one hour slowly lowers the EXP, but never to zero Category level   EXP needed for the next level 1–3   1 10   3 20   7 30   14 40   27 50   51 59   90

Some category levels need Research before they can go up. When the EXP bar is full at one of these levels, start Research on the skill page and wait for the timer. Every category has research steps except Survival. Category level   Research time 20   5 minutes 25   20 minutes 30   1 hour 35   2 hours 40   4 hours 45   12 hours 50   24 hours 55   48 hours 59   72 hours You can research one category at a time Research can only start while the category level is below your character level While researching, keep doing that category's work to shorten the timer (EXP × category level ÷ 10 seconds per action), up to 25% of the total time

Total Skill Points = 10 + (character level − 1) × 5 Character level   Total Skill Points 1   10 10   55 20   105 40   205 60   305 Skill ranks cost different amounts. Some ranks cost 0 points and are learned automatically once the category level is reached Ranks must be learned in order, and the category level must meet the rank's requirement A sub-skill needs its main skill first

Learn: open the Skill page, choose a category and learn the next rank. Your character must be alive. Skill Rewind: removes one rank at a time, starting from the top rank, and refunds the points right away. A main skill cannot be removed while any of its sub-skills are still learned. Rewind number that day   Cost 1–5   Free 6–15   1 Skill Rewind Voucher (if you have one), otherwise 30 T-Stones Over 15   Not possible until the reset The quota resets every day at 22:00 Thai time (UTC+7), which is 15:00 UTC.

You pick a career when you create your character. A career gives three things: One category starts at Lv.20 1–5 starting skill ranks in that category Starting items, one piece per line, at the level shown Career   Category at Lv.20   Starting items   Points used by starting skills Soldier   Melee   Ruined Tag Lv.10 · Survival Food · Modern Banknote ×2   3 Job Seeker   Defense   Ruined Keyboard Lv.10 · Modern Banknote ×2   2 Office Worker   Construction   Ruined Modern Hammer Lv.10 · Blue Bull Lv.20 · Modern Banknote ×3   6 Engineer   Weapon/Tool   Ruined Folding Chair Lv.10 · Rope Lv.20 ×2 · Modern Banknote ×2   8 Attendant   Tailoring   Ruined Modern Needle Lv.20 · Thread Lv.20 ×2 · Modern Banknote ×2   10 Farmer   Farming   Ruined Modern Hoe Lv.10 · Ruined Bucket Lv.10 · Corn Seed · Modern Banknote ×2   7 Chubu (homemaker)   Cooking   Ruined Bucket Lv.10 · Ramen · Modern Banknote ×2   5 Student   Gathering   Ruined Baseball Bat Lv.10 · Modern Banknote ×2   7 Starting skills count as points already spent. For example, an Attendant starts the game with 10 of 10 points used. [!tip] Your Lv.20 career category will not grow again until your character passes Lv.20, because a category cannot go above your character level. Level your character first.

The Career Guide button is on the skill page. It holds 58 courses, grouped by line and by difficulty 1–4. Each course is a list of skills to learn. Pick a course as your target Learn the listed skills until the course reaches 100% Claim the reward: items plus the course's title Line   Courses Combat   13 Weapon Crafting   13 Tailoring   8 Cooking   8 Construction   6 Gathering   6 Farming   4 Difficulty   Courses   Skill Points needed 1   7   17–31 2   13   27–71 3   19   44–157 4   19   104–264 At Lv.60 (305 points) you can finish any course, even the most expensive one (264). [!tip] A title from a course is yours forever. Rewinding skills to learn another line does not remove it, so you can collect titles from several lines one after another.

d: Earn titles from the Career Guide, organizations and character level. Wear one at a time, others can see it, and it gives stat bonuses

Only the title you are wearing gives a bonus. Changing or removing it updates the bonus right away. You can check the numbers on your character's Detailed Stats page. The 8 base stats: Strength · Charisma · Dexterity · Agility · Endurance · Will · Intelligence · Perception Endurance +1 = max health +2 Will +1 = max energy +0.8 Special bonuses (some titles): Bonus   Effect Max health   Raises your real health cap Max energy   Raises your real energy cap Health regeneration   Restores health every second Accuracy   Raises accuracy on the stats page Crafting ability of a line   Raises that value on the stats page Example title   Base stats   Special bonus Basic Hunting Tactics (Career Guide, difficulty 1)   Strength +5 · Endurance +5   Max health +40 → +50 max health in total One-Handed Combat: Criminal Psychology (difficulty 4)   Strength +30   Health regeneration +1.5 per second Kitchen Management (difficulty 4)   Charisma +30   Cooking ability +4 Apex Predator (event)   All stats +30   Max health +150 · health regeneration +2 · accuracy +20 · max energy +50 [!tip] Difficulty-1 Career Guide titles are the easiest to get (17–31 Skill Points), and many of them add max health. They are a good pick early in the game. d: Team up with other players, set up ranks, share land and storage, donate to the clan funds to level the clan up, and form alliances with other clans.

sec.x: Clan A clan is a permanent group of players. It has a leader, ranks, its own chat room, and shared Clan Enclaves and storage. The more members donate to the Clan Funds, the higher the clan level: more members, more alliance slots, and a buff that reduces what you drop when you die.

Create your own clan, or ask to join an existing one Set up ranks, name them, and choose what each rank may do Talk in the clan chat (works across all islands) Wear a clan honour flag on your back Declare a Clan Enclave and build/share storage there by rank Donate T-Stones to the Clan Funds → clan level goes up Form alliances with other clans Run clan research at a research center (paid from the Clan Funds)

Open the Clan menu → Create Clan → pick a name and pay the creation cost Or search for a clan and press Request to Join — wait for someone with the right to approve you (you can cancel your request) If someone invites you, a message appears on screen — go to that clan and request to join; you get in at once without approval Item   Value Creation cost   5,000 T-Stones Clan name   2–16 characters · must be unique Clans per character   1 at a time Clan notice / introduction   up to 300 / 500 characters Clan emblem image   up to 4 KB Leaving: if the leader leaves, leadership passes to the next-highest rank (same rank = whoever joined first). If the last member leaves, the clan is disbanded — all Clan Enclaves and the buildings on them go to that last leader. [!warn] When a clan is disbanded, the T-Stones in its Clan Funds are lost. They are not refunded.

A new clan has 3 ranks. The default rank names are in Thai (หัวหน้า / รองหัวหน้า / สมาชิก); the leader can rename them. Rank   Permissions Leader (หัวหน้า)   Everything · rename the clan · manage alliances · hand over leadership Vice leader (รองหัวหน้า)   All 5 permissions: approve applicants · change ranks/kick · edit clan info · manage Clan Enclaves · research Member (สมาชิก)   No special permissions You can add ranks, up to 10 ranks in total · rank names 1–12 characters · ranks can be reordered by dragging Someone with the rank-change permission can only manage members of a lower rank · nobody can kick or demote the leader If the leader gives someone the leader rank, leadership is handed over (the old leader drops to the next-highest rank) Deleting a rank moves its members to another rank automatically
The Clan chat channel reaches members on every island You can switch notifications on or off per channel; the server remembers your choice (default = all off)

Clan flag Clan members can wear a flag on their back that others can see. There are 3: The Strong · The Mighty · The Unbreakable. This server has no clan wars, so every member may wear any of them. Leaving, being kicked, or the clan disbanding removes the flag automatically.

The leader, or a rank allowed to manage enclaves, can declare a Clan Enclave on a stable island · it can be expanded up to 8 cells (whoever presses expand pays the cost) Members can build on the Clan Enclave, and members' buildings don't count as someone else's property there Default rights on a Clan Enclave: leader/enclave managers = everything · members = enter, use, put in, take out, build (no dismantling) — the leader can change rights per rank Each box/warehouse can be set per rank, including how many items a rank may take per day (unlimited / none / a set number · counted over 24 hours) The server keeps a log of who put in or took what from boxes on the Clan Enclave (latest 300 entries per clan) General land rules: Land · boxes: Storage · wear and tear: Decay

d: Trade with other players at the Market for T-Stones and buy from the Shop with T-Stones — this server has a single currency and no real-money top-ups.

sec.x: T-Stone The main currency on this server is T-Stones. You use them to trade with other players at the Market, buy things in the Shop, pay for cargo, create a clan, and more. This server has no real-money top-ups — everything is bought with T-Stones earned in the game.

List items from your bag at the Market at your own price Search/filter listings and buy what others are selling Star listings you like to keep them in Favorites Collect money from sales · take back items that didn't sell Buy packages, random boxes, items and tickets in the Shop

Wallet This server uses a single wallet: T-Stones. Currency   Used for T-Stones   Main money — Market, Shop, cargo fees, clan creation, Clan Funds, etc. · you can hold up to 99,999,999 Loyalty   Separate points given as a bonus by some Shop items — spent in the Loyalty Shop Tickets   Some things are tickets (e.g. map-opening tickets), kept separately in your wallet Some Shop items show their price with a Gem/Coin icon — on this server they cost the same number of T-Stones (1 to 1), and the balance shown under the Gem/Coin icons is your T-Stone balance. Where T-Stones come from: discovering new places on the map and full-exploration rewards · Quests · daily attendance · mini-games · Warp · gift mail (Mail) · selling at the Market

Open the Market menu → Sell tab Pick items from your bag (equipped or locked items can't be listed) Set the price per item and how long to sell → confirm — the items leave your bag right away While on sale you can press Cancel Listing at any time; the item returns to your bag You can pick several items at once; each is listed separately at the same price You sell the actual item — the buyer gets its durability, color and tags as they are Food on the Market does not spoil while listed (see Preserving)

Search by name, category, tag, price range and level range; sort by price, time, level or durability Many screens have a shortcut to search the Market, e.g. material slots when building/repairing Press Buy → pay T-Stones, the item goes straight into your bag · you can't buy your own listings Star listings to keep them in Favorites — the server remembers them after you log out

d: Ship items home through Courier Warp Holes, board a catapult, fly a balloon and ride animals — for travelling between islands see the Islands page.

sec.x: Courier Warp Hole (Exit) This page covers moving goods and vehicles on this server. Send items home from any island → Courier Warp Holes Vehicles available now → the Catapult (boarding only) · balloons at camps · riding pets Travelling to other islands → see Islands and Warp

No need to carry loot home yourself — send it from a Warp Hole to an exit you built. Catapult The only vehicle you can sit in on this server is the Catapult — touch it and press Board to get on, Dismount to get off. Travelling to another island, dying or disconnecting dismounts you automatically. There is no Catapult blueprint to learn yet (only ones placed by admins/events), and it cannot fire yet.

Some camps have a balloon station — touch it to board for free and fly freely over water and mountains · you can only land at spots where landing is allowed. d: Your mailbox receives gifts, update news, unsold Market items and items from other players — collect everything at once with Receive All.

sec.x: Gift Mail is where items and news from the server arrive — welcome gifts, update news with attachments, unsold Market items, and items other players send you. Attached items, T-Stones and tickets are not added to your bag until you receive them.
Open and read mail Receive attachments one mail at a time, or Receive All Delete mail you have already collected, or that has no attachments

Press the mail icon on the main screen — a notification dot appears when new mail arrives, and the server sends your mailbox as soon as you log in. The mailbox has 2 sides: System (mail from the server) and Player (items other players sent you). Select a mail → read it Press Receive — items go to your bag, T-Stones/tickets to your wallet Press Delete — only mail with nothing left to collect can be deleted (otherwise you're told to receive it first) Attached items are the actual items — you get their durability, color and tags as they were
The Receive All button collects every automatic mail at once (welcome, update news, gifts). Mail sent by the staff by hand is highlighted — open it first, then Receive All will include it.

The Player side receives items other players send you, e.g. a thank-you gift after you revive someone — if you are not online at that moment, it comes by mail instead, so nothing is lost.

d: Island types (Ancora, Safe House, Tamed Island, Unstable Islands, Civilized Islands) · sailing, balloons, returning to a Stable Island · island levels, Unstable Index and danger

sec.x: The world of Durango is an archipelago. Every island has its own level and climate. Some islands are safe and permanent (you can settle there), others are Unstable Islands — more dangerous, but with better loot. Everyone on the server shares the same world: you meet, help and compete with other players on the same islands. An Unstable Island on the sailing map

Start on Ancora → build a raft → arrive at The Company's Safe House Take the Hot Air Balloon to claim your own Tamed Island, then declare a Domain Sail from a Harbor to Unstable Islands in 8 climates, level 15–60, to gather and hunt Pick your own difficulty with each island's Unstable Index (1–10) Go home for free at any time with Sail to the last Stable Island or the warp buttons on Warps & Rifts

Type   Island level   Domain   Unstable Index   Island fatigue Ancora (starting island)   1   No   1 (stable)   None The Company's Safe House   5   No   1 (stable)   None Tamed Island   10   Yes (free expansion)   1 (stable)   None Unstable Island   15–60   No   1–10   Yes Training island (tropical)   18   No   1 (stable)   Half Civilized Island (abandoned city)   40   Yes   1 (stable)   Half Event islands   20–60   No   1   Yes

Every new character starts on Ancora — the tutorial island, rebuilt from the original game's real map. Follow the tutorial, finish the raft (4 logs · 6 reed stems) and it carries you to the Safe House. Ancora has 4× the usual resources · depleted resources come back 4× faster · resting recovers fatigue 3× faster You can sail back to visit Ancora from a Harbor, but you can only leave by raft — you must build it again every time

The hub for new players — K and the Company's staff, a workbench, a campfire, a notice board, a Harbor, a balloon station and Warp Holes you can use right away without finding them. If you haven't set a Waypoint anywhere, the Safe House is your "home".

A level 10 grassland island for settling down — declare a Domain, build a house, farm, raise animals. Expanding a Domain on a Tamed Island is free. No bosses, and no climate fatigue from the island itself. Tamed Islands are a shared world — everyone who picks the same island layout lives on the same island. You see each other and can visit each other's homes, like a village where everyone stakes out their own plot. Spots already declared show as owned, so look for the next free one. Your first trip to your Tamed Island is by Hot Air Balloon from the Safe House (see Hot Air Balloon below). Right now there is only one layout to pick — coming soon: 5 layouts (end of page).

Islands you reach by sailing — high-level resources and aggressive animals. Most islands of level 35 and above have Rifts and craters. The higher the level or Index, the more dangerous. You cannot declare Domains here. Island names are shown in Thai on this server, even in the English client.
A level 18 tropical island with the survival tutorial (find a crater, find the harbor). You can sail there from any Harbor. Its Index is always 1, it has no predators, and island fatigue is halved.
Four abandoned cities at level 40 (grassland · temperate · tropical · tundra) — stable islands where you can declare a Domain. Island fatigue is halved.

Islands from the original game's past events (grassland festival · Summer Club · Season 1/2 islands) are open as normal islands with Index 1. If you log out while on an event island, you'll wake up at home next time (see "Logging out on a temporary island" below).

Walk to a Harbor and tap it → choose Sail The sea map opens — pick a climate/level, then an island by the Index you want Confirm "Do you want to move to the … island?" → you land at that island's arrival point Sailing is free — no T-Stones — and islands are not level-locked. You can go to a level 60 island at level 1, but you'll tire very fast Islands with Index 3 or higher need enough climate resistance (table below), or you can't set sail Your pets and everything in your bag come with you

At the Harbor of an Unstable Island you get Sail to the last Stable Island and "Return to the Tamed Island harbor you started from?" — both take you straight to your home island, for free. Home island = the island where you used Designate as Waypoint (your own bed/tent) · never set = the Safe House Leaving any island clears that island's automatic checkpoint (a bed/tent Waypoint is kept)

Hot Air Balloon The balloon station at the Safe House offers two things: Leave — go to your Tamed Island (the first time, the Declare Tamed Island screen opens first) Board Hot Air Balloon — fly freely over the island, even across water. Free to board · flights last up to 15 minutes, then you land automatically · you can't land on water/cliffs — you'll be sent back to the station

The higher the Index, the tougher the animals and the faster you tire — but mission exp and the latent properties on what you gather get better too. sec.h: Logging out on a temporary island
sec.x: If you log out or disconnect while on a temporary island — an Unstable Island with Index 2+, an event island, or the training island — the next time you log in you'll be on your home island (or the Safe House) with the message "The island disappeared and you were moved to your Waypoint." Everything you carry and your pets come with you. Stable islands (Safe House · Ancora · Tamed Island · Civilized Islands · Unstable Islands with Index 1) → you come back where you were Arriving on a temporary island by boat doesn't move you — it only happens on the next login after you log out A single island whose Index rotates to 2+ while you're offline counts as temporary too

On Unstable Islands with Index 2 or higher, every crater becomes a resource cache — 10 natural resources of one kind around the crater (5-tile radius), guarded by 3 animals that are ×1.5 tougher than normal (on top of the island's Index). The cache type depends on the island's climate, e.g. iron mine, rubber trees, fir forest.

Warp Hole Warp Holes exist on Unstable Islands level 35–60, Civilized Islands, event islands and the Safe House — islands level 15–30, the training island and Tamed Islands have none. Explore until you find a Warp Hole — the first time you find one you get a discovery reward You need to find at least 2 Warp Holes on the same island before you can warp ("You need to find at least two Warp Holes to use them.") Warp Accelerator A Rift is a crack in the ground leaking Warp energy. There are 4 per island (6 on Volcano islands) on Unstable Islands level 35–60 (except Deep Swamp), the temperate/tropical/tundra Civilized Islands and some event islands — none on level 15–30 islands, Tamed Islands or the Safe House.

Tap an idle Rift → start the Warp Accelerator, paying the 1,000 T-Stone entry fee — everyone on the island gets an announcement Friends have 10 seconds to tap the Rift and join (also 1,000 T-Stones · within 10 tiles of the Rift · up to 10 players) Each tier, guard animals (the island's predators) appear around the Rift in 2 waves — clear them all within 60 seconds After a tier you get a 15-second break, then the next tier starts, up to 10 tiers · from tier 3, Allosaurus join the waves Run out of time = the run ends · tap the Rift to collect rewards within 2 minutes (once per player) · failing tier 1 = no reward The Rift then rests for 3 minutes before a new run can start Leaving the island or disconnecting mid-run removes you from the run — no reward for that run If starting/joining fails, your T-Stones are refunded Tier   Animals per tier (1 player)   Animals per tier (4 players) 1   3   5 3   5   9 5   7   12 10   12   20 Animals = (2 + tier) × (1 + 0.25 × (players − 1)), at most 20 per tier
